body.x: Ninewatt (CEO Youngrok Kim) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.
Ninewatt provides an energy management platform that analyzes power consumption patterns and tariff structures based on building energy data and presents practical cost-reduction strategies.

The platform goes beyond simply displaying electricity usage. It conducts an integrated analysis of multiple factors, including contracted power capacity, peak load, tariff plans, and equipment operating methods. Based on these results, it proposes intuitive solutions that enable building managers to make rational, informed decisions.

In particular, Ninewatt has recently advanced the performance and reliability of its AI-based analytics engine. Through this, the company positions its platform as an “energy advisor” that enables building managers to manage energy with minimal resources.

By learning from both historical and real-time data, the platform detects abnormal usage patterns and provides operation guides optimized for each situation. This agent-based technology is expanding across diverse environments, including public institutions, private buildings, and industrial facilities.

Ninewatt’s Opti platform, which represents what the company calls “Building Energy Intelligence,” was selected as an Innovation Award winner in the Smart Communities category at CES 2026 and will be introduced at the event as a cutting-edge solution enabling intelligent energy management.

Opti is designed to access smart meter data at 15-minute intervals without requiring additional hardware installation, collecting and analyzing power usage patterns in near real time. Through wireless communication networks, it collects data from smart meters and further analyzes climate conditions, tariff plans, and building load characteristics. Based on this, the platform supports usage forecasting and evaluates the effectiveness of investments in facilities such as solar power systems and energy storage systems (ESS).

Ease of use is another key strength of the Opti platform. It offers a web-based dynamic dashboard that displays real-time energy flows, cost forecasts, and simulation results. In addition, a conversational interface built on large language models enables users to interact through natural language commands and questions. For example, when a user asks, “How much can electricity costs be reduced by adjusting power usage during peak hours?”, the platform provides insights such as projected billing scenarios and adjustment measures derived through high-precision simulations.

A Ninewatt official said, “By showcasing Opti, which provides practical advice and concrete action plans for reducing energy consumption, we aim to demonstrate our world-class technological competitiveness and attract the interest of potential customers and partners.” The official added, “We also plan to explore networking opportunities with companies, institutions, and investors in the energy management field for future domestic and overseas collaboration.”

The official continued, “At the same time, we will identify new trends across industries and technologies related to intelligent building energy management, such as AIoT, digital twins, and ESS, explore opportunities to integrate these technologies into our solution, and further refine Ninewatt’s technology roadmap.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
